fatal_errors: The central intervention—a 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder in ZrB2—is omitted.
The proposed 1700–1900 °C SPS window misses the tested 1300–1600 °C range and the 1500 °C optimum.
The hypothesis assumes single-phase ZrB2, so it cannot reproduce the binder-mediated pore filling, grain connection, or binder overflow at 1600 °C.
No supporting evidence is cited, and improved oxidation resistance is asserted although the target study principally measured molten-Al corrosion and wear rather than oxidation.
explanation: The response recognizes SPS as a lower-temperature consolidation method and proposes sensible density, microstructure, mechanical, oxidation, and liquid-metal measurements. However, SPS alone is not the target intervention. The target depends on adding 30% AlFeNiCoCr binder and optimizing SPS temperature: binder fluidity improves pore filling and bonding through 1500 °C, whereas binder loss at 1600 °C increases porosity. Consequently, the generated mechanism, processing boundaries, baselines, and predicted optimum do not match. Its experiment is broadly falsifiable but uses wide processing ranges, does not compare 1300/1400/1500/1600 °C cermets, and fails to specify molten Al at 700 °C for up to 12 days or the associated wear test. It is therefore a generic, potentially plausible SPS alternative rather than a reconstruction of the supported hypothesis.
